title: Hosea Bible Quiz - Chapter 4
description: Ten questions on Hosea 4: the charge against the inhabitants of the land, the people destroyed for lack of knowledge, and Ephraim joined to idols.

questions.text: What does Yahweh say is missing in the land, in his charge against its inhabitants?
questions.explanation: The verse says there is no truth, nor goodness, nor knowledge of God in the land.

answers.text: Truth, goodness and knowledge of God

questions.text: Which creatures are named as wasting away or dying with the land?
questions.explanation: The verse says the land will mourn and everyone in it waste away, with the animals of the field, the birds of the sky, and the fish of the sea also dying.

answers.text: The flocks, the herds and the beasts of burden
The animals of the field, the birds of the sky and the fish of the sea
The lions, the jackals and the wild donkeys
The doves, the eagles and the creeping things

questions.text: For what reason does Yahweh say his people are destroyed?
questions.explanation: The verse says my people are destroyed for lack of knowledge, and because they rejected knowledge he will also reject them.

questions.text: What short saying does this chapter use about the people and the priest?
questions.explanation: The verse says it will be like people, like priest, and that he will punish them for their ways and repay them for their deeds.

questions.text: What does this chapter say takes away understanding?
questions.explanation: The verse says prostitution, wine and new wine take away understanding.

questions.text: Under which trees does the chapter say they burn incense on the hills?
questions.explanation: The verse says they sacrifice on the tops of the mountains and burn incense on the hills, under oaks and poplars and terebinths, because its shade is good.

answers.text: Under palms and cedars and olive trees
Under oaks and poplars and terebinths
Under vines and fig trees and pomegranates
Under willows and myrtles and almond trees

questions.text: Which two places is Israel told not to come to in this chapter?
questions.explanation: The verse says do not come to Gilgal, neither go up to Beth Aven, nor swear, as Yahweh lives.

questions.text: What is Israel compared with because of its extremely stubborn behavior?
questions.explanation: The verse says Israel has behaved extremely stubbornly, like a stubborn heifer.

questions.text: What does this chapter say about Ephraim and idols?
questions.explanation: The verse says Ephraim is joined to idols, and adds the words, leave him alone.

answers.text: Ephraim has broken his idols in pieces
Ephraim has hidden his idols in the hills
Ephraim has sold his idols to the nations
Ephraim is joined to idols, so leave him alone

questions.text: What has wrapped her up in its wings, in the last verse of the chapter?
questions.explanation: The verse says the wind has wrapped her up in its wings, and they will be disappointed because of their sacrifices.
